test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 15 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given, followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements

**Statements:**

1. All cars are scooters.

2. All scooters are trucks.

3. No helicopter is truck.

**Conclusions:**

I. No truck is scooter.

II. All cars are trucks.

III. Some trucks are scooters.

IV. No car is helicopter.

options.text: Only either conclusions I or IV follow and III follow
Only conclusions II, III and IV follow
Only either conclusions I or IV follow

solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/73d54e4529eed8f826b8983cfde7495e382786f9a621e60f134045d97dc84619.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No truck is scooter → **Does not** follow (As all scooters are trucks. As whole scooters comes in trucks, therefore it is false)

II. All cars are trucks → Follow (As all cars are scooters and all scooters are trucks. As whole cars comes in scooters which whole comes in trucks, therefore it is true.)

III. Some trucks are scooters → Follow (As (As all scooters are trucks. As whole scooters comes in trucks, therefore it is true)

IV. No car is helicopter → Follow (As all cars are scooters, all scooters are trucks and no helicopter is truck. As whole cars comes in scooters which whole comes in trucks which cannot be helicopter, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusions II, III and IV follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3"
